# The `pdf` format (package `document`)

This reference covers `document` versions `>=1.3.1, <2.0.0`. Compare with the version
`dre plugin list` shows (in a project, `dre.lock` pins it); outside that range, say its
options may differ from this list before relying on it.

## Profile fields

None: a format has no profile. Its options go in the report's `output:` block, or for
the whole project under `format_options.<format>` in `dre_project.yml`.

## Report options

Set in the report's `output:` block.

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_rows` | integer | no | `50000` | min 1.0 | the most rows across the output's queries; more fails the run |
| `page_size` | string | no | `A4` | `A3`, `A4`, `A5`, `Letter`, `Legal` | paper size, used when the template's CSS sets no `@page` size |
| `orientation` | string | no | `portrait` | `portrait`, `landscape` | used when the template's CSS sets no `@page` size |
| `margins` | string | no | `20mm` |  | page margins as in CSS, like `20mm` or `15mm 20mm`; used when the CSS sets no `@page` margin |
| `author` | string | no |  |  | the PDF's author metadata |
| `subject` | string | no |  |  | the PDF's subject metadata |
| `password` | string | no |  |  | an open password: the PDF is encrypted with AES-256 and opens only with it; Jinja like `{{ each.pdf_password }}` |
| `missing_fonts` | string | no | `warn` | `warn`, `error` | when a script's font can't be fetched (offline, nothing cached): `warn` makes the PDF with boxes for its characters and warns once per script per run; `error` fails the output (each row, per row) instead |

## From the plugin docs

### PDF and HTML documents

A client statement, a board pack or a compliance summary: one HTML + CSS template, filled with
the report's query results, written as an `.html` file or laid out into a `.pdf`. The PDF is made
inside the plugin: no browser, no Playwright, no conversion service and no network call. *New in
DRE 0.6.* The package needs DRE 0.6.0 or later.

##### A statement

```yaml
#### reports/clients/statement/statement.yml
queries: [summary, holdings]
vars:
  client: Acme Pty Ltd
sets:
  - {name: acme}
  - {name: beta, vars: {client: Beta Ltd}}
output:
  format: pdf
  template:
    file: statement.html          # found next to this YAML (see "Finding a template")
  author: Acme Funds
```

```html
<!-- reports/clients/statement/statement.html -->
{% extends "base.html" %}
{% block title %}Statement for {{ var('client') }}{% endblock %}
{% block body %}
<h1>{{ var('client') }}</h1>
<p>Balance on {{ run.date | date('d mmmm yyyy') }}:
   <strong>{{ results.summary.first.balance | currency('AUD', 2) }}</strong></p>
{{ table(results.holdings) }}
{% include "terms.html" %}
{% endblock %}
```

```html
<!-- reports/clients/base.html: shared by every report in the folder -->
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en-AU">
<head>
  <title>{% block title %}{% endblock %}</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/brand.css">
  <style>
    @page { size: A4; margin: 20mm 15mm;
            @bottom-center { content: "Page " counter(page) " of " counter(pages); } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <img src="assets/logo.svg" alt="Acme">
  {% block body %}{% endblock %}
</body>
</html>
```

`dre run statement --set all` writes `statement.pdf` for each Set. Change `format: pdf` to
`format: html` for a web page from the same template. With no `template:`, the output is a plain
document with a table per query.

##### What a template reads

Everything a [message](../docs/messages.md#what-a-message-template-reads) template reads, the same way:

| | |
|---|---|
| `results.<query>` | each query of the output, in YAML order: `value`, `first.<column>`, `rows`, `row_count`, `columns`, `column_types` (each column's type, `{amount: Decimal128(18, 2)}`), `sets[n]` |
| `var('name')` | every resolved var: `--var`, the schedule's, the Set's, the report's, its folders' and the project's, whether or not a query uses it |
| `run.*`, `target.name` | the report, Set, date, timezone and the rest of [`run`](../docs/templates.md) |
| `locale` | the run's [`locale:`](../docs/templates.md#locale) tag, for `<html lang>` |

Values keep their types: numbers stay numbers, dates are DRE dates (shown in the run's timezone),
nulls are `none`. Unlike messages, `rows` holds every row: a document is never cut short (see
`max_rows`). `env_var()` isn't available: a document is data that's delivered.

Filters and functions:

- The [number filters](../docs/templates.md#numbers-number-percent-signed-currency-compact): `number`,
  `percent`, `signed`, `currency` and `compact`, in the run's `locale:`, as in messages.
- `date(format)`: a date or timestamp in an Excel-style format (`dd/mm/yyyy`, `d mmm yyyy`,
  `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm`); default `yyyy-mm-dd`.
- `row.fmt('amount')` (on a row of `rows`, or `first`) shows a value in its column's YAML
  `format`, the [xlsx format codes](../docs/plugin-xlsx.md#column-formats) (`$#,##0.00`, `d mmm yyyy`);
  a column with no format is shown as `table()` shows it. `row.amount` stays the raw value, for
  comparisons and arithmetic.
- `table(results.<query>)` writes a styled `<table class="dre-table">` of the query's rows, each
  value shown with its column's YAML `format` (the [xlsx format codes](../docs/plugin-xlsx.md#column-formats),
  such as `$#,##0.00` or `d mmm yyyy`). `table(results.q, ['fund', 'amount'])` picks and orders
  the columns. Style it with CSS on `.dre-table`.
- The date functions (`date()`, `period()`, ...) of [every template](../docs/templates.md).

Values are HTML-escaped, so a client called `A&B <Ltd>` shows as written; `| safe` inserts
deliberate markup. A value that isn't there (`results.holdings.first.amout`) fails the run,
naming the template line and the queries and columns there are, so a statement never goes out
with a silent blank. Project macros (`macros/`) aren't available here: share layout with
`{% include %}` and `{% extends %}`.

##### Finding a template

`template.file`, `{% include %}`, `{% extends %}` and `{% import %}` find a file the same way:

- A name with `/` is a path from the project root, taken exactly: `templates/statement.html`.
- A bare file name is looked for next to the report's YAML (for an include: next to the
  including template), then in each parent folder up to the project root; the nearest wins.
- Failing that, anywhere in the project, where it must be unique. Two matches are an error that
  lists both; name one by its path.

Never outside the project, and never a URL. The same rule finds an [xlsx](../docs/plugin-xlsx.md#start-from-a-complete-workbook-project)
template. A Set can override `template.file` like any other output key, so one client can get a
different layout.

##### Images, stylesheets and fonts

`<img src>`, `<link rel="stylesheet" href>` and CSS `url()` are relative to the template that
writes them (a shared `base.html` links its logo next to itself), and must be inside the project.
`http(s)://` is refused: rendering is offline and gives the same document every time. PNG, JPEG,
GIF and SVG images work, and so does inline `<svg>`, so a logo or a simple chart made by a macro
appears in the PDF.

An `html` output is one self-contained file: its images, stylesheets and fonts are inlined as
data URIs, so it still shows its logo after email, S3 or SFTP delivery. `embed_assets: false`
keeps them as links, for a file published next to its assets.

The PDF uses only fonts it's given, never the machine's, so it looks the same everywhere. The
plugin bundles **IBM Plex Sans** (regular, bold, italic) and **IBM Plex Mono**, under the SIL Open
Font License. Add your own with `@font-face`, from a `.ttf` or `.otf` file in the project:

```css
@font-face { font-family: Brand; src: url(fonts/Brand-Regular.ttf); }
@font-face { font-family: Brand; src: url(fonts/Brand-Bold.ttf); font-weight: bold; }
body { font-family: Brand, sans-serif; }
```

A `font-family` that's neither bundled nor declared falls back to IBM Plex Sans, with a warning
naming it. Fonts are subset: the PDF holds only the characters it uses.

###### Fonts for other languages

From `document` 1.3.0, PDF text in Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Korean, Arabic,
Hebrew, Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali) and Thai needs no project fonts when used with a core
that supports font requests. Before laying out the PDF, the plugin checks its characters against
Plex and the project's `@font-face` fonts. For each script they leave uncovered, core fetches
that script's **Noto Sans** regular and bold, and only those: a Hindi report downloads Devanagari
and nothing else. Arabic and Hebrew run right to left, Arabic letters join, and Devanagari forms
its conjuncts (`नमस्ते`).

Project fonts stay first when explicitly selected. Other declared project families are available
as fallbacks after Plex, including outside elements that select them; Noto is the final fallback.
HTML behavior stays the same: the reader's browser supplies missing fonts, and DRE never
downloads Noto for HTML. The [multilingual example](https://github.com/get-dre/dre/blob/master/examples/multilingual/README.md) makes a
PDF letter in each of nine languages this way.

###### Han characters follow `lang`

Chinese, Japanese and Korean share the Han characters (`直`, `東京`) but draw many of them
differently. As in a browser, the HTML `lang` attribute of an element, or of its nearest ancestor
that has one, picks the font: `ja` Japanese, `ko` Korean, `zh` Simplified Chinese, and `zh-Hant`,
`zh-TW`, `zh-HK` or `zh-MO` Traditional Chinese. Set it once for the whole document, or per
element:

```html
<html lang="ja">
  <p>東京本社</p>
  <td lang="zh-TW">臺北</td>
</html>
```

In a per-row report, set it from the row, with no new YAML key:

```html
<td lang="{{ each.lang }}">{{ each.city }}</td>
```

Text with no Chinese, Japanese or Korean `lang` (none, or another language such as `en`) is
guessed from the document: kana (`です`) means Japanese, Hangul (`한국어`) means Korean, and Han
characters alone mean Simplified Chinese. That last guess adds a one-line note suggesting `lang`.
CSS generated content (`content:`) follows the `lang` of `<html>`.

###### Pinned versions and the cache

The registry pins each package with a SHA-256 checksum for each weight and its SIL Open Font
License 1.1 text:

| Script | Package | Version | Upstream |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Japanese | `noto_sans_jp` | 2.4.0 | Noto Sans CJK JP 2.004 |
| Simplified Chinese | `noto_sans_sc` | 2.4.0 | Noto Sans CJK SC 2.004 |
| Traditional Chinese | `noto_sans_tc` | 2.4.0 | Noto Sans CJK TC 2.004 |
| Korean | `noto_sans_kr` | 2.4.0 | Noto Sans CJK KR 2.004 |
| Arabic | `noto_sans_arabic` | 2.13.0 | Noto Sans Arabic 2.013 |
| Hebrew | `noto_sans_hebrew` | 3.1.0 | Noto Sans Hebrew 3.001 |
| Devanagari | `noto_sans_devanagari` | 2.7.0 | Noto Sans Devanagari 2.007 |
| Thai | `noto_sans_thai` | 2.2.0 | Noto Sans Thai 2.002 |

Font files are not bundled in the plugin or added to the project. Core keeps verified files and
the licence in `~/.dre/fonts/<package>/<version>/`; a second run uses this cache without
contacting the registry. `DRE_REGISTRY_URL` mirrors cover fonts as well as plugins. Older cores
keep their previous PDF behavior, and older document plugins keep working with newer cores.

###### Offline servers

A run fetches each font once, and only when the cache doesn't have it. On a machine that can't
reach the registry, any of these makes the fonts available:

1. **An offline copy of the registry.** Copy `packages.json` and its font files, point their
   `url`s at the copies, and set `DRE_REGISTRY_URL` to the index (a plain path, a `file://` URL
   or an internal `https://` mirror), as for plugins ([registry](../docs/registry.md#the-registry)).
2. **`dre fonts install` on a connected machine.** It downloads and verifies fonts into
   `~/.dre/fonts` ahead of time, by script or language: `dre fonts install ja zh-Hans ar`, or
   `--all`. Copy `~/.dre/fonts` to the offline machine, or run it in the Docker image build.
   `dre fonts ls` lists what's cached. It installs each package's newest version in the
   registry, which the current `document` plugin pins (the table above); an older plugin may
   pin an older one.
3. **The project's own fonts**, declared with `@font-face` (above). They always come first, and
   a script they cover never needs a download.

```dockerfile
RUN dre fonts install ja ko ar
```

Otherwise the PDF is still made, with boxes for the characters of each script DRE has no font
for, and the run warns once per script, however many PDFs or rows need it:

```
   Warning    row `1`: pdf format: no Japanese font for this PDF, so its Japanese text shows as boxes (can't read /srv/registry/packages.json: No such file or directory (os error 2)). To fix it, set `DRE_REGISTRY_URL` to an offline copy of the registry, run `dre fonts install ja` on a connected machine and copy its `~/.dre/fonts` here, or add a font covering Japanese to the project with `@font-face`
```

A run tries the registry once per font: after a failure, its other PDFs don't wait for it again.

###### Failing instead: `missing_fonts`

For PDFs that must never show boxes, `missing_fonts: error` fails the output instead of making
the PDF (each row's, for a per-row output); the error names every script without a font and the
same fixes. The default is `warn`. `dre validate` rejects other values, and the option is for
`format: pdf` only: HTML uses the reader's fonts.

```yaml
output:
  format: pdf
  template: {file: statement.html}
  missing_fonts: error
```

Text inside an SVG is the exception: it's drawn with the machine's fonts. For a logo that looks the
same everywhere, convert its text to outlines (paths) in your design tool, or write the name in
the html next to an icon-only SVG.

##### Page setup

Set the page in CSS, as for print: `@page { size: A4 landscape; margin: 15mm }`, page-margin boxes
for running headers and footers (`@top-right`, `@bottom-center` with `counter(page)` and
`counter(pages)`), and `break-before: page`, `break-after`, `break-inside: avoid`. A table that
runs over several pages repeats its `<thead>` on each. The `page_size`, `orientation` and
`margins` options apply only where the CSS sets nothing.

The PDF's title comes from `<title>`, its language from `<html lang>`, `author` and `subject`
from the options, and its creation date is the run's `run.now`, so the same data makes the same
file.

##### How big a document can be

`max_rows` (default 50,000) caps the rows across every query of one document. More fails the run
with a hint, before anything is laid out: aggregate in SQL, filter, or raise it. A message
instead keeps its first `max_rows` rows; a document fails, because it must never be cut short.
A single table of more than about 30,000 rows is more than the layout engine handles: split it,
or aggregate. Laying out 5,000 table rows takes about a second.

##### Checks before a run

`dre validate` (and `dre run`, before any query) parses the template and every file it includes
by a literal name, checks its images and stylesheets exist, its filters exist, and that each
`results.<name>` is a query of the output, with a "did you mean" hint. An include whose name is
computed (`{% include "terms/" ~ var('client') ~ ".html" %}`) gets a warning that it isn't checked
until the run.

##### Designing a template

A template takes many tweaks. Save the results once, then re-render from them, with no query and
no connection, in about a second:

```bash
dre run statement --set acme --no-deliver --output-json design   # runs the queries once
dre run statement --set acme --from-results design               # each tweak: re-render only
```

`--from-results` reads the results `--output-json` saved (`design/<report>/<binding>/`, see
[the manifest page](../docs/manifest.md)), renders every output of the report (xlsx and messages too),
and implies `--no-deliver`. It fails when a query has no saved result, and warns when a query's
SQL changed since they were saved.

###### What the PDF engine draws differently

The PDF is laid out by [fulgur](https://github.com/fulgur-rs/fulgur), not a browser, so check a
design in the PDF itself. One difference: a box's borders share one colour, its top border's. For
a coloured line on one side only, set the colour for every side and the width for that side:

```css
header { border: 0 solid #e8873a; border-bottom-width: 2pt; }
```

##### Password-protected PDFs

`password:` on a `pdf` output encrypts the file after it's laid out: it opens only with that
password. AES-256 (PDF 2.0), with a random owner password nobody keeps, so the encryption can't
be lifted with a blank owner password. *New in `document` 1.1.0.*

```yaml
output:
  - name: statement
    format: pdf
    template: {file: statement.html}
    for_each: {query: members, key: member_id}
    password: "{{ each.pdf_password }}"        # or "{{ env_var('STATEMENT_PW') }}"
```

- The password is Jinja like other output values: `each.*` for one per row, `env_var()`, `var()`.
  A templated password needs DRE 0.7.0 or later; a literal one works on 0.6.
- An empty password is an error, never an unencrypted file. `html` takes no password: zip it
  with a password on the destination instead ([zip packs](../docs/password-protected-outputs.md)).
- Keep passwords to ASCII letters, digits and punctuation: macOS Preview and Safari can't open a
  PDF whose password has other characters (Acrobat, Chrome, Edge and Firefox can). The run warns.
- Mark the password's column in [`secret_columns:`](../docs/password-protected-outputs.md#keep-passwords-out-of-dres-records) so it never shows in
  DRE's logs, results or previews, and send the password by another route than the file.
- Only an open password: no print, copy or edit restrictions (readers honour those voluntarily).

##### Delivery

File destinations send a `.pdf` as `application/pdf` and an `.html` as `text/html`; an email
attachment opens in the recipient's mail client. To email the document, attach the output to a
message with [`attach:`](../docs/messages.md#a-headline-plus-the-file).

### Formats

Each format plugin declares and checks its own options: `dre validate` and `dre run` send every
report's `output:` keys to the plugin before anything runs, and report each problem with the
report it came from. A format no declared package provides, or whose package isn't installed, is
an error. For one no declared package provides, `dre validate` and `dre run` look it up in DRE's
plugin registry and name the package to add under `plugins:` in `dependencies.yml`.

Project-wide defaults for a format go in `dre_project.yml` under `format_options`, keyed by
format. They apply under every output of that format, whatever folder or report chose it, and a
report's own keys win:

```yaml
format_options:
  delimited: {delimiter: "|", quoting: strings}
  csv: {quoting: all}
```

| Format | Options |
|---|---|
| `csv`, `delimited` | `delimiter`, `quote`, `quoting`, `header`, `line_ending`, `encoding`, `null`, `byte_order_mark` |
| `fixed_width` | `columns` (see [Fixed-width columns](../docs/plugin-fixed_width.md#columns)), `header`, `line_ending`, `encoding`, `line_breaks` |
| `parquet` | none; Arrow types are preserved |
| `xlsx` | `header`, `max_rows_per_sheet`, `autofit` (see [Column widths](../docs/plugin-xlsx.md#column-widths)), `style` (see [Styles](../docs/plugin-xlsx.md#styles)), `columns`, `date_format`, `datetime_format`, `time_format` (see [xlsx column formats](../docs/plugin-xlsx.md#column-formats)), `totals_label` (see [xlsx formulas and totals rows](../docs/plugin-xlsx.md#formulas-and-totals-rows)); per query `anchor`/`header`/`autofit`/`style`/`columns`; `template` |
| `html`, `pdf` | `max_rows`; html `embed_assets`; pdf `page_size`, `orientation`, `margins`, `author`, `subject`, `password`; `template` (see [PDF and HTML documents](../docs/plugin-document.md)) |
| `message` (built in, no plugin) | `text` or `file`, `title`, `max_rows` (see [The `message` format](../docs/plugins.md#the-message-format)) |

Every format but xlsx also takes `extension`: the output file's extension (`aba`, `dat`, ...), or
`""` for none. The file is written the same way; only its name changes.

- Timestamps with a timezone are written in their zone with the offset,
  `2026-01-01 11:00:00+11:00`; timestamps without one as `2026-01-01 00:00:00`.

## Guide notes

- A branded PDF from a Jinja HTML + CSS template, made in-process: no browser, no service. The
  same template makes the `html` format; see the `document` plugin page.
- Page setup goes in CSS: `@page { size: A4; margin: 20mm; @bottom-center { content: "Page "
  counter(page) " of " counter(pages) } }`, `break-before: page`. Long tables repeat `<thead>`.
- Fonts: IBM Plex Sans/Mono are bundled; add brand fonts with `@font-face` from a `.ttf` in the
  project. System fonts are never used; an unknown family falls back with a warning. Other
  scripts (Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Thai) get a Noto font fetched on
  first use and cached; set `<html lang>` (or `lang` on an element) so Han text picks the right
  one, `missing_fonts: error` to fail rather than draw boxes, and `dre fonts install` for offline.
- Assets (`<img>`, stylesheets) are files in the project; URLs are refused.
- `max_rows` (default 50,000) fails the run rather than truncate; aggregate in SQL.
